page: OVHcloud l40s-90 is a GPU-accelerated cloud instance belonging to the Cloud GPU family, provisioned through the KVM hypervisor. The instance is driven by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9124 processor clocked at 2.75 GHz, configured with 15 dedicated physical cores and 15 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation stands at 90.0 GB of system RAM, providing 6.0 GB per core. The hardware foundation features an NVIDIA L40S accelerator based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, equipped with 48 GB of dedicated VRAM. Storage includes 400 GB of local NVMe SSD space, while network connectivity delivers an 8 Gbps baseline throughput without bundled complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional machine learning capabilities enabled by the onboard NVIDIA L40S GPU. In large language model inference tests, the instance ranks in the top tier (top 10%), achieving 13,644.94 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 135M model, 6,030.41 tokens per second on a 7B model, and 884.03 tokens per second on a 70B model. For text generation, throughput reaches 605.12 tokens per second on the 135M model, 136.71 tokens per second on the 7B model, and 15.72 tokens per second on the 70B model. Host CPU performance presents a contrast: single-core performance scores in the top 25% across Geekbench (1,941.0) and stress-ng (3,043.17), while multi-core metrics sit squarely in the middle 50% with a PassMark CPU score of 34,459.04 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,588.0.

The primary tradeoff of the l40s-90 lies in its host-to-accelerator balance. While the 48 GB Ada Lovelace GPU provides premier throughput for inference pipelines, the local storage footprint of 400 GB NVMe limits massive on-node dataset caching. Memory bandwidth and compression metrics, such as bzip3 multi-threaded decompression at 184.98 GB/sec and uncached memory read bandwidth at 49.41 GB/sec, align with middle 50% expectations. The system offers high compute efficiency for GPU-centric operations rather than host-heavy data manipulation. The instance is best suited for generative AI inference, deep learning model fine-tuning, high-throughput LLM serving, and graphic or ray tracing rendering workloads.
